Triggers.value: When people say things like my ex

Maladaptive Strategies.value: make sure to stay close to exit
Situations in which other people evaluate me / my appearance / my performance
wear concealing clothing to avoid being noticed

Threat.value: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard
My body feels constantly tense and ready to react to danger

Negative Appraisals.value: Somebody else would not have gotten into this situation
I used to be a happy person but now I am always miserable.
I feel permanently humiliated by what happened

issues.explanation: 'Heavy make-up' is hard to reconcile with this patient's demographics (22-year-old single male auditor) and the rest of the profile unless there is a specific unreported context such as concealment or gender expression. In this profile it stands out as clinically implausible relative to the other items, whereas the other maladaptive strategies center on vigilance, escape, and social evaluation.

vignette: Amir's eyes scan the crowded coffee shop, his gaze darting towards the exit before returning to his laptop screen. It's a habit he's developed over the past year, ever since the night he was raped by someone he trusted. The smell of freshly brewed coffee wafts through the air, transporting him back to that fateful evening. He recalls the scent of the perpetrator's cologne, and his stomach twists into knots. To cope with the wave of anxiety that follows, Amir instinctively adjusts his hoodie, making sure it's securely zipped up to conceal his body. This is just one of the many strategies he's adopted to avoid drawing attention to himself. As an auditor, Amir's job requires him to interact with strangers on a daily basis. However, since the assault, he finds himself avoiding unfamiliar places and situations where others might evaluate him or his appearance. He becomes fixated on potential dangers lurking in every corner, his body perpetually tense and ready to react to sudden movements. His colleagues have noticed a change in him, but Amir is too ashamed to open up about his experiences. When they ask how he's doing, he shrugs it off, fearing that if they knew the truth, they'd judge him or worse – pity him. When people around him misbehave or disregard basic social norms, Amir feels a surge of moral outrage, which serves as a painful reminder of his own powerlessness during the assault. He begins to question whether he was somehow complicit in what happened, wondering if someone else would have been more vigilant or proactive in defending themselves. This self-doubt festers, fueling his conviction that he's permanently humiliated by the experience. Amir starts to believe that if only he had been stronger, more assertive, or more worthy, this wouldn't have happened. As the days turn into weeks, Amir becomes increasingly withdrawn, avoiding social gatherings and public events where he might encounter triggers. He sticks to familiar routines and environments, never venturing far from exit routes or safety nets. However, even these coping mechanisms can backfire – in his attempts to avoid evaluation, he inadvertently draws attention to himself by being overly cautious or evasive. His colleagues start to notice his avoidance behaviors and begin to wonder what's wrong with him. One day, while working on a project, Amir overhears a coworker making a flippant comment about someone else's appearance. The remark hits close to home, echoing the degrading comments his perpetrator made during the assault. Amir feels like he's been punched in the gut, and his body goes into high alert. He hastily packs up his things and makes a beeline for the door, desperate to escape the toxic atmosphere. As he steps out into the bright sunlight, he realizes that even in his attempts to avoid danger, he may have inadvertently created more – by avoiding unfamiliar places, he's also limiting his opportunities for healing and growth. Amir knows he can't keep living like this, constantly looking over his shoulder, expecting the worst from himself and others. He fears that if he doesn't confront these demons head-on, they'll consume him entirely. With a mix of trepidation and determination, Amir schedules an appointment with a therapist, hoping to break free from the suffocating grip of shame and self-doubt that has haunted him for far too long.
